Samira — great to connect earlier. Summary and next steps below.

Short answer: based on the workload you described (peaks to ~1.2k rps and tight 99th latency goals), we typically recommend starting with Redwood Dedicated for the POC and then evaluating Private VPC if you need stricter compliance or on-prem. Hosted API can work for experimentation but may require rate/fallback policies for production peaks.

Why Dedicated first:
- Provides a reserved GPU pool (single-tenant) which eliminates co-tenant noisy neighbor interference for the capacity you reserve.
- Predictable kernel scheduling and KV cache residency for your model — reduces tail variance.
- Fast path for rolling model changes and autoscaling policies with guaranteed burst capacity options.

Private VPC/on-prem is the right call if you have strict audit/KMS requirements or must keep traffic inside your network. That has longer lead times (typically 4–8 weeks for VPC onboarding, longer for on-prem).

Isolation & noisy neighbor mitigations we recommend:
- Dedicated pools: single-tenant GPU pools with isolated scheduling, GPU memory reservations, and limits on background work. This is the most straightforward way to remove noisy neighbor risk.
- Admission control + traffic shaping: prefix-aware routing and token-bucket shaping to avoid sudden unbounded spikes.
- KV/prefix caching pinning: we can configure your model to reserve KV cache shards for warm sessions to mitigate cold-start tail latency.
- SLO alignment: we'll work with your SREs to set realistic 99th latency targets and define fallbacks (smaller model variant, cached fallthrough) for overload.

SLOs & guarantees: for Dedicated customers we offer configurable latency SLOs tied to instance sizing and SLA packages. Typical commitments we see for workloads like yours: 99th latency in the 200–450 ms range depending on model size and seq length, with dedicated sizing. We can run a workload profile to give a tighter number.

Proposed next steps (suggested timeline):
1) POC scoping call (this week) — 30–45 min to capture traffic patterns, auth/KMS requirements, and sample inputs.
2) Baseline profiling run (we ask for a 10–20 min traffic capture or synthetic profile): we’ll run offline sizing and provide recommended instance counts and a Dedicated pool config.
3) 2-week Dedicated POC: we provision a Dedicated pool, run live traffic (you can route a share of traffic) and collect latency/cost metrics.
4) Decision: move to Dedicated committed capacity or accelerate to Private VPC.

I attached a short comparison deck with empirical notes and a worksheet for traffic profiling. Also linking our deployment comparison (internal).
